(a) ferricyanide is a good final electron acceptor for beta-oxidated intermediates, and (b) oxaloacetate stimulates the rate of beta oxidation by rat liver mitochondria but not by heart or kidney mitochondrias.
(1) a rapid and sensitive spectrophotometric assay for beta-oxidative fatty acid metabolism was developed and (2) oxaloacetate is a potent stimulator of beta-oxidative flux in intact mitochondria.
the reduction of ferricy anide by acyl-CoA-dependent beta-oxidation can be measured spectrophotometrically.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a rapid and sensitive assay for beta-oxidative activity in intact mitochondria.
the study of the mechanisms of beta-oxidization of long chain fatty acids.
the development of a spectrophotometric technique for the direct measurement of beta-oxidative metabolism in intact mitochondria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate of oxidation of fatty acids by intact mitochondria can be determined rapidly by using the spectrophotometric method described.
the rate of beta oxidation by heart mitochondria is limited by the rate of oxidation of acetyl-CoA to CO2 and water.
the rate-limiting factor(s) for beta-oxidative fatty acid oxidation is (are) not the acyl-Coenzyme A dehydrogenases, but rather the availability of the acyl-CoAs and of the electron transport chain.

the beta-oxidation rate of heart mitochondria can now be measured without interference by the oxidation of trcarboxylic acid cycle intermediates.

the rate of beta oxidation can be limited by the availability of substrates other than acyl CoAs, such as acetyl CoA, oxaloacetete, malate or succinate.
